record.paper_title: Analysis on Faddeev Knots and Skyrme Solitons: Recent Progress and Open Problems
record.original_question: In the geometric Skyrme model for maps from the three-sphere S^3_R of radius R into the unit three-sphere S^3, there is a threshold R0 ∈ (√3/2, √2] such that for R < R0 the identity map x/R is the unique minimizer. Can this threshold be taken to be exactly √2?

evidence.quote: More recently, Riviere proved in [68] that, for the geometric Skyrme model governing maps from S3_R into S3, there is an R0 ∈ (√3/2, √2] such that for R < R0, the identity map x/R remains to be the unique minimizer. Whether or not one can take R0 to be equal to √2 remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^3_R \subset \mathbb{R}^4$ denote the round 3-sphere of radius $R>0$, and let $S^3$ denote the unit 3-sphere. For a sufficiently regular map $\varphi: S^3_R \to S^3$, define the geometric Skyrme energy
$$E(\varphi) = \int_{S^3_R} \left( |d\varphi|^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}|d\varphi \wedge d\varphi|^2 \right) dV_{g_R},$$
where $|d\varphi|^2$ is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the differential and $|d\varphi \wedge d\varphi|^2$ is the squared norm of the wedge of $d\varphi$ with itself, both computed using the round metric $g_R$ on $S^3_R$ and the round metric on $S^3$. The identity (rescaled) map $\mathrm{id}_R : S^3_R \to S^3$, $x \mapsto x/R$, is a critical point of $E$ in the topological class of degree-one maps.

It is known that there exists a threshold $R_0 \in (\sqrt{3}/2, \sqrt{2}]$ such that for every $R < R_0$ the map $\mathrm{id}_R$ is the unique minimizer of $E$ among degree-one maps. Determine whether one can take $R_0 = \sqrt{2}$; that is, decide whether for every $R < \sqrt{2}$ the identity map $x \mapsto x/R$ is the unique minimizer of the geometric Skyrme energy among degree-one maps $S^3_R \to S^3$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of whether the threshold $R_0$ for uniqueness of the identity as the minimizer of the geometric Skyrme energy on $S^3_R$ can be taken equal to $\sqrt{2}$. Existing literature on the Skyrme model on Riemannian manifolds discusses the identity-map minimization phenomenon, but no source confirming or refuting the sharp value $R_0=\sqrt{2}$ was located.

status_evidence.title: The Skyrme Model on Riemannian manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Under certain assumptions it is shown that the identity map is essentially the only absolute minimizer ... In some other circumstances, it is shown that the identity map is a stable local minimum.
status_evidence.claim: Background showing the identity-map minimization question on Riemannian 3-manifolds is studied, but the sharp threshold $R_0=\sqrt{2}$ on $S^3_R$ is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Recent mathematical developments in the Skyrme model
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of analytic results on Skyrme-type energies.
status_evidence.claim: No update settling the sharp threshold question was found in surveys of recent Skyrme-model analysis.
